arxiv-2103-03878.title: Some further q-shift difference results on Hayman conjecture
arxiv-2103-03878.creator: Goutam Haldar
arxiv-2103-03878.description: Abstract . In this paper, we investigate the zero distributions of q q -shift difference-differential polynomials of meromorphic functions with zero-order that extends and generalizes the classical Hayman results of the zeros of differential polynomials to q-shift difference. We also investigate the uniqueness problem of q q -shift difference-differential polynomials sharing a polynomial value with finite weight.

arxiv-2105-09799.title: Higgs boson decays with lepton flavor violation in the ​ B − L \emph{B-L} symmetric SSM
arxiv-2105-09799.creator: Ze-Ning Zhang 1 , Hai-Bin Zhang 1,2 , Jin-Lei Yang 1,3 , Shu-Min Zhao 1,2 , and Tai-Fu Feng 1,2,4
arxiv-2105-09799.description: Abstract Recently, the ATLAS and CMS Collaborations reported the latest experimental upper limits on the branching ratios of the lepton flavor violating (LFV) 125 GeV Higgs boson decays, h → e ​ μ h\rightarrow e\mu , h → e ​ τ h\rightarrow e\tau , and h → μ ​ τ h\rightarrow\mu\tau .

arxiv-2106-15542.title: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive GANs for Medical Image Translation
arxiv-2106-15542.creator: Uddeshya Upadhyay, Yanbei Chen, Tobias Hepp, Sergios Gatidis, Zeynep Akata
arxiv-2106-15542.description: Abstract Image-to-image translation plays a vital role in tackling various medical imaging tasks such as attenuation correction, motion correction, undersampled reconstruction, and denoising. Generative adversarial networks have been shown to achieve the state-of-the-art in generating high fidelity images for these tasks.

arxiv-2201-08135.title: Survey on Federated Learning Threats: concepts, taxonomy on attacks and defences, experimental study and challenges Journal: Information Fusion
arxiv-2201-08135.creator: Nuria Rodríguez-Barroso, Daniel Jiménez López, M. Victoria Luzón, Francisco Herrera, Eugenio Martínez-Cámara
arxiv-2201-08135.description: Abstract Federated learning is a machine learning paradigm that emerges as a solution to the privacy-preservation demands in artificial intelligence. As machine learning, federated learning is threatened by adversarial attacks against the integrity of the learning model and the privacy of data via a distributed approach to tackle local and global learning.

arxiv-2306-09619.title: Early-times Yang-Mills dynamics and the characterization of strongly interacting matter with statistical learning
arxiv-2306-09619.creator: Matthew Heffernan, Charles Gale, Sangyong Jeon, Jean-François Paquet
arxiv-2306-09619.description: Abstract In ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions, a plasma of deconfined quarks and gluons is formed within 1 1 fm/c of the nuclei’s impact. The complex dynamics of the collision before ≈ 1 \approx 1 fm/c is often described with parametric models, which affect the predictivity of calculations.

arxiv-2404-19758.title: Invisible Stitch: Generating Smooth 3D Scenes with Depth Inpainting
arxiv-2404-19758.creator: Paul Engstler, Andrea Vedaldi, Iro Laina, Christian Rupprecht
arxiv-2404-19758.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Paul Engstler, Andrea Vedaldi, Iro Laina, Christian Rupprecht. 3D scene generation has quickly become a challenging new research direction, fueled by consistent improvements of 2D generative diffusion models. Most prior work in this area generates scenes by iteratively stitching newly generated frames with existing geometry. These works often depend on pre-trained monocular depth estimators to lift the generated images into 3D, fusing them with the existing scene representation.

arxiv-2409-01574.title: Policy Gradients for Optimal Parallel Tempering MCMC
arxiv-2409-01574.creator: Daniel Zhao, Natesh S. Pillai
arxiv-2409-01574.description: Abstract Parallel tempering is a meta-algorithm for Markov Chain Monte Carlo that uses multiple chains to sample from tempered versions of the target distribution, enhancing mixing in multi-modal distributions that are challenging for traditional methods. The effectiveness of parallel tempering is heavily influenced by the selection of chain temperatures.

arxiv-2409-07709.title: Harnessing TI Feeds for Exploitation Detection
arxiv-2409-07709.creator: Kajal Patel 1 , Zubair Shafiq 1 , Mateus Nogueira 4 , Daniel Menasché 4 , Enrico Lovat 2 , Taimur Kashif 1 , Ashton Woiwood 3 , Matheus Martins 2
arxiv-2409-07709.description: Abstract Many organizations rely on Threat Intelligence (TI) feeds to assess the risk associated with security threats. Due to the volume and heterogeneity of data, it is prohibitive to manually analyze the threat information available in different loosely structured TI feeds. Thus, there is a need to develop automated methods to vet and extract actionable information from TI feeds.

arxiv-2509-01755.creator: Subhadip Paul
arxiv-2509-01755.description: Abstract Anemia is a global health concern, prompting the need for rapid and accurate diagnostic tools, especially for vulnerable populations. Estimating the blood lysis level (LL) and oxygen saturation (SO 2 ) are essential not only for anemia but also for other hemolytic conditions.

arxiv-2510-24420.title: A model of trees for 5-connected planar triangulations Thanks: ∗ LIGM, CNRS, Univ Gustave Eiffel, ESIEE Paris, F-77454 Marne-la-Vallée, France, eric.fusy@univ-eiffel.fr
arxiv-2510-24420.creator: Éric Fusy ∗
arxiv-2510-24420.description: Abstract . Triangulations of the 5-gon with no separating triangle nor quadrangle, so called 5c-triangulations, are a planar map family closely related to 5-connected planar triangulations. We show that 5c-triangulations are in bijection with 5-regular plane trees satisfying a simple local constraint at inner edges.

pmc-11437081.description: This study presents the development and characterization of a novel nanocomposite wound dressing material based on polylactic acid (PLA) nanofibers incorporating chitosan nanocapsules loaded with chamomile extract and cellulose nanoparticles. The nanofibers were fabricated using a three-step synthesis and electrospinning techniques, resulting in uniform, bead-free fibers with an average diameter of 186 ± 56 nm.

pmc-11456945.title: Comparison of Clinical Outcomes of Posterior-Only Transforaminal Debridement and Interbody Fusion With Preservation of Posterior Ligamentous Complex Versus Conventional Posterior-Only Debridement and Interbody Fusion for Thoracic Spine Tuberculosis: A Prospective, Randomized, Controlled, Clinical Tr

pmc-11499544.title: The role of MRI in radiotherapy planning: a narrative review “from head to toe”
pmc-11499544.creator: Simona De Pietro, Giulia Di Martino, Mara Caroprese, Angela Barillaro, Sirio Cocozza, Roberto Pacelli, Renato Cuocolo, Lorenzo Ugga, Francesco Briganti, Arturo Brunetti, Manuel Conson, Andrea Elefante
pmc-11499544.description: Over the last few years, radiation therapy (RT) techniques have evolved very rapidly, with the aim of conforming high-dose volume tightly to a target. Although to date CT is still considered the imaging modality for target delineation, it has some known limited capabilities in properly identifying pathologic processes occurring, for instance, in soft tissues.

pmc-12464266.title: Decoding of image properties from single-trial visual evoked potentials recorded by ultra-high-density EEG
pmc-12464266.creator: Sebastian Sieghartsleitner, Leonhard Schreiner, Johannes Grünwald, Michael Jordan, Rossella Spataro, Josef Scharinger, Christoph Guger
pmc-12464266.description: Visual evoked potentials (VEPs) recorded by encephalography (EEG) allow us to study the neuronal activity non-invasively and in high temporal resolution. Traditionally, EEG analyses have relied on univariate group-level statistics and trial averaging to detect effects. However, recent advances in high-density EEG enable the investigation of brain responses at the single-subject and single-trial level.

pmc-12530093.title: From bench to bedside and back: translational cardiovascular interventions in veterinary medicine
pmc-12530093.creator: Sebastian Popiel-Dziewierz, Agnieszka Noszczyk-Nowak, Artur Dziewierz
pmc-12530093.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Veterinary interventional cardiology exemplifies the power of reverse translation in cardiovascular medicine. This review examines how procedures initially tested in animal models, refined in human medicine, and subsequently reintroduced to veterinary practice have completed the translational cycle.

pmc-13028689.title: The Senolytic Drug Navitoclax Protects the Brain After Experimental Ischemic Stroke
pmc-13028689.creator: Dianoush Falahatgaroshibi, Júlia Baixauli-Martín, María C. Burguete, Mikahela A. López-Morales, Alicia Aliena-Valero, José E. Peris, Juan B. Salom
pmc-13028689.description: Background/Objectives: Senescence has been recently described in brain cells following ischemic stroke. The potential of targeting senescence as an effective therapeutic approach in the treatment of ischemic stroke requires further investigation. This study evaluated the effects of the senolytic drug navitoclax after experimental ischemic stroke.
